Resources

This is the shelf where I keep the useful stuff. Not more articles to read, but actual tools: the things my family pays for and uses, the guides I put together because I needed them myself, and, before long, a few small paid ones you can buy. Everything here has to earn its spot. If I wouldn't hand it to a friend across my kitchen table, it doesn't go on this page. And if a link pays me, I say so right next to the link, every time.

What my family actually uses

CrowdHealth (opens in a new tab) (health sharing, code NORMAL). We're a family of four, and we left regular health insurance for this. It's a flat monthly fee plus a share of other members' bills, and they make their money on the fee instead of on slow-walking your claim. Join through my link and your first 3 months are $99 a month. CrowdHealth pays me $250 once you've been a member in good standing for 3 months. It costs you nothing extra, and now you know exactly what I make on it.

Now the honest other half, because it matters more than the discount. CrowdHealth is not insurance. Nobody is legally on the hook to pay your bill. It has waiting periods, exclusions, and rules about conditions you already have. For some families it's the wrong answer, full stop. Read who health sharing is wrong for before you read anything else about it, and read the plain-English guide if the whole idea is new to you.

River (opens in a new tab) (buying bitcoin). This is where I buy. It's a US company, bitcoin only, no dozens of coins to get distracted by, and you can set up a small automatic buy every week and then leave it alone. That's the whole point for me. Saving, not trading. River splits a referral bonus between us, in bitcoin, and it's the same amount on both sides. We each get $5 when you buy your first $100, another $15 each at $1,000, and another $80 each at $10,000. That caps out at $100 apiece. It isn't offered in every state, so check their terms before you count on it.

Same honesty rule here. Bitcoin's price jumps around a lot, and it can go down and stay down for a long while. Only put in money you can leave alone for years. If you're brand new, read Saving vs. Gambling: Where Bitcoin Actually Fits first, then Your First $20 in Bitcoin, Step by Step.

Book a call with me

Sometimes a blog post can't do the job. If you're staring at a specific hospital bill, weighing whether health sharing fits your family, or trying to sort out a money decision that's bigger than an article, I take on a few people a month for one-on-one help.

There's no fancy booking calendar yet. Just send me a note, pick "One-on-one help," and tell me what's going on. I'll write back with whether I can actually help you and what it would look like. If I'm not the right person, I'll tell you that too, and point you somewhere better. No pressure, no sales call.

What's coming

I'm building a few small paid things: simple worksheets and step-by-step guides for the stuff people email me about, like reading a hospital bill line by line and setting up a family budget that survives a real month. They'll show up here when they're good, not before. If there's something you'd pay ten bucks to never have to figure out again, tell me and I'll probably build that first.
